extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment analysts, health policy stakeholders, measure developers, and other CMS program stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards used in the FY2027 IPPS proposed rule covering wage-index caps and transitional exceptions, FTE and cost-report handling for DGME/IME and NAH, measure development/review processes, and selection/definition choices for quality measures (e.g., sepsis readmission measure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index cap policy (0.95 floor per FY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the wage index cap policy at 42 CFR 412.64(h)(7), a hospital's wage index for a FY cannot be lower than 0.95 * its wage index from the prior FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied year-to-year: e.g., 90.25% = 0.95 * 0.95 for two years; over three years the floor would be 0.95^3 (85.7375%). Used to limit year-to-year decreases in a hospital's wage index.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY2027 transitional exception significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital is considered 'significantly impacted' by discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy if its FY2027 wage index is less than (0.95 * 0.95 * 0.95) of its FY2024 wage index (equates to a decrease of more than 14.2625 percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold mirrors the cumulative effect of the annual 5% floors over three years (.95^3). The proposed transitional exception would be applied for FY2027 to hospitals meeting that criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application mechanics of FY2027 transitional exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is not proposing to change the FY2027 wage index values under section 1886(d)(3)(E) for hospitals eligible for the proposed FY2027 transitional exception on the basis of the exception; the proposed change will be applied as a separate step only for purposes of determining the hospitals' FY2027 IPPS payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transitional exception is functionally equivalent to adjusting FY2027 payments and can alternatively be considered a transitional adjustment. Scope/magnitude will be much smaller than prior policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRMR voting options and consensus threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: As of 2025 the PRMR committee members will vote either 'recommend' or 'do not recommend' that a measure be added to the intended CMS program(s); the 'recommend with conditions' option has been removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold to reach consensus on a given measure continues to be a minimum of 75 percent agreement among members. Committee members may provide considerations for CMS to review prior to implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reevaluation of implemented measures
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS conducts an annual reevaluation of measures implemented in its quality reporting and value-based purchasing programs to ensure they remain valid and reflective of current clinical practice and coding standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of reevaluation, CMS may update measure cohorts, risk adjustment models, or outcomes as appropriate. Updates are informed by review of recent scientific literature, stakeholder input, empirical analyses, and assessments of coding trends indicating shifts in clinical practice or billing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability guidance for endorsement/maintenance of clinical quality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure developers/maintainers should follow the Reliability Guidance for the Endorsement and Maintenance of Clinical Quality Measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers readers to the Reliability Guidance document (available at p4qm.org/em/resources) for more details on reliability expectations used in endorsement and maintenance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sepsis measure definition selection (Sepsis-2 vs Sepsis-3 tradeoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the proposed sepsis readmission measure, CMS elected to align the measure with the Sepsis-2 definition to ensure cases were not missed, while ensuring no overlap with existing condition- and procedure-specific 30-day readmission measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale explained: Sepsis-2 is highly sensitive (identifies patients earlier), Sepsis-3 is highly specific (risks missing patients). The selection reflects expert clinical and TEP input favoring sensitivity for the measure's intended purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost report selection for calculating Factor 3 (uncompensated care)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining Factor 3 for a FY, CMS uses the cost report that spans the entirety of that FY to determine uncompensated care costs for that FY, and the hospital's most recent prior cost report (that spans some portion of the prior FY) to determine uncompensated care costs for the prior FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For FY2019, use the cost report that spans FY2019 for FY2019 calculations and the most recent prior cost report that spans some of FY2018 for FY2018 calculations. CMS will not use the same cost report for both FYs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling aberrant or missing cost reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If a cost report is determined to include potentially aberrant data, CMS will use the subsequent cost report for the ratio calculation. If a hospital lacks a cost report for a given FY because an earlier cost report spanned that FY, CMS will use the earlier report that spans the FY and chain backwards for prior-year data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If FY2018 report is aberrant, use FY2019 report. If no FY2021 report because FY2020 report spanned FY2021, use FY2020 report for FY2021 and then use FY2019 report if it spans part of FY2020. CMS will not use the same cost report to represent two different FY time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration application for FTE counts and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Proration factors are applied after prior- and penultimate-year FTE counts have been determined based on data from the respective cost reports and consistent with instructions to lines 12 and 13 of Worksheet E-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For short cost reporting periods or proration needs, calculate prorated caps (e.g., DGME cap prorated: cap ÷ 365 × number_of_days_in_reporting_period) and then compare to actual weighted FTE counts to determine the applicable prior-year FTE count.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGME FTE cap and prior-year FTE computation for short cost reporting periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior-year DGME FTE count equals the lesser of the DGME FTE cap or the actual weighted FTE count during the period, plus any podiatric or dental FTEs (as applicable). For short cost reporting periods the DGME FTE cap is prorated (cap ÷ 365 × days_in_period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: cap of 25 prorated for a 304-day period = 25 ÷ 365 × 304 = 20.82; compare to weighted FTE (e.g., 16.55) to choose the lesser value as the prior-year DGME FTE count.

rubrics_metrics.name: IME FTE computation for merged/terminating providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-merger IME numerator is the lesser of each hospital's IME FTE cap or actual IME FTE count, plus any podiatric and dental FTEs, during the respective periods; counts from surviving and terminating providers are added and reported as though merged for the entire cost reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hospitals merge, FTE caps and adjustments of surviving and terminating providers are combined and reported on applicable FTE cap lines as though merged for the entire cost reporting period. Available bed days of terminating non-teaching providers are included in the post-merger count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of FTEs for merged hospitals training displaced or new-program residents
rubrics_metrics.description: If any merged hospital is training displaced residents or residents in the initial years of a new program, those weighted counts are determined according to the same procedure and the FTEs are added to the respective rolling averages calculated for the pre- and post-merger periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent procedures for calculating and adding FTE counts across pre- and post-merger periods; apply proration if reporting periods are nonstandard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider-operated NAH training cost eligibility for pass-through payment (§413.85)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §413.85(f)(1)(i), the provider itself must directly incur the training costs in order for a program to be deemed provider-operated and thus eligible for pass-through payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cautions related parties about incurring NAH training costs (including indirect costs), as that could jeopardize the provider's status as the operator of the program and eligibility for pass-through payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and treatment of related-party overhead costs associated with NAH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: General service costs incurred by a related party are reported on Worksheet A-8-1. If the hospital reports related party overhead costs associated with an NAH program on Worksheet A-8-1, it must create an additional subscript for each corresponding general service cost center containing only those related party costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overhead costs incurred by a related organization and allocated to NAH cost centers would be removed as a post-stepdown adjustment on Worksheet B-2; such costs are not paid on a pass-through basis but instead are allowable as normal operating costs of the hospital and included in the prospective payment rates.
